$additions_from_slice_159.go_sqlc_generate_diff_required: Slice 159 promoted `Go · sqlc generate diff` to required-checks, closing slice 109 anti-criterion P0-A3. The job was added by slice 109 with `continue-on-error: true` as an informational signal — the promotion was deferred until the install paths were proven byte-identical between the brew-distributed binary contributors install and the `go install`-built binary CI uses. Drift surfaced 2026-05-18 during slice 153's PR #330 (first PR whose path filter triggered the real job rather than the docs-only stub). Slice 159 root-caused the drift to structural sqlc v1.31.1 inferencer limits on `CASE WHEN ... (scalar subquery)::bigint END` (policies.sql) and `CASE-WHEN-aggregate-over-LEFT-JOIN` with redundant explicit casts (scf_anchors.sql) — NOT install-path divergence (Option A in the slice doc). Fix was Option C (SQL query rewrite): `policies.sql` switched to a CTE+LEFT-JOIN pattern that emits `*int64`; `scf_anchors.sql` dropped the redundant `::evidence_result`/`::text` outer-SELECT casts so sqlc sees the LEFT-JOIN nullability flow through and emits `*EvidenceResult`/`*string`. Handlers in `internal/api/policies/handlers.go` and `internal/api/anchors/handlers.go` switched from sqlc's `.Valid`/`.Int64`/`.EvidenceResult`/`.String` wrapper API to pointer-style nil-check + dereference. JSON response shape on `GET /v1/policies?include=ack_rate` and `GET /v1/anchors?include=state` is unchanged. After merge: run `bash scripts/apply-branch-protection.sh` to push the contexts list to live GitHub branch-protection. AC-10 (synthetic-drift PR) is the merge-time evidence the gate actually blocks; see `docs/audit-log/159-sqlc-toolchain-ci-drift-fix-decisions.md`.

$slice_158_drift_detector_redesign: Slice 158 (PR #311 follow-on) redesigned the drift-detector CI surface introduced by slice 127. PR #311's wrong fix added `administration: read` to the GITHUB_TOKEN permissions block; `administration` is not a valid scope, actionlint flags it, GHA silently rejected the workflow file at parse, and slice 127's drift detector never actually ran. Slice 158 fixes the root cause: the PR-time job (`branch-protection-drift-validate`) validates only the file shape (no `gh api` call, no elevated token), and a separate push-on-main job (`branch-protection-drift-live`) does the live compare using `secrets.BRANCH_PROTECTION_READ_TOKEN` (fine-grained PAT with `Administration: Read` scope, env-scoped to the one step that needs it). Slice 158 also adds an actionlint pre-commit + CI guard so the same invalid-scope mistake cannot recur. The required-checks contexts list is UNCHANGED by this slice — both new jobs remain informational, matching the slice 127 P0-A1 posture. See `docs/adr/0005-branch-protection-pat-vs-app.md` for the PAT-vs-App D1 decision + maintainer setup steps.

$retain_advisory_from_slice_419.self_host_bundle_end_to_end_stays_adviso: RETAINED ADVISORY — `Self-host bundle · end-to-end` (slice 065, ci.yml jobs `test-self-host-bundle` L1143 / `test-self-host-bundle-stub` L1222) is deliberately NOT promoted by slice 419. This is a decision with two independent reasons, not an accident (P0-419-2 / threat I-1).
$retain_advisory_from_slice_419.reason_1_structural_context_name_mismatc: DECISIVE. The real job is a 4-leg matrix (`mode: [bundled, external, proxy, migrate]`) and GitHub reports it under the MATRIX-EXPANDED names `Self-host bundle · end-to-end (bundled)` / `(external)` / `(proxy)` / `(migrate)`. The base name `Self-host bundle · end-to-end` is reported ONLY by the slice-061 stub, i.e. only on docs-only PRs. Verified empirically over the window: 33 stub reports under the base name, 0 real reports under it. Adding the base name to `contexts` would therefore NEVER resolve on a code PR and would brick every code merge (P0-419-3). Adding the four expanded names instead requires four NEW matrix-named stub-twins so docs-only PRs still resolve them — the ci.yml block at L1135 already anticipates this ('Promote it to a required check (and add the matrix-named stubs) in a follow-up'). Those four stubs cannot be exercised in BOTH directions inside this slice (this PR is docs-only, so only the stub path runs; a code PR would exercise only the real path), so shipping four unverified required contexts is exactly the never-resolves failure P0-419-3 forbids.
$retain_advisory_from_slice_419.reason_2_soak_not_clean_D1: CORROBORATING. 4 of the 5 red candidate legs in the whole window are this job. One is a TRUE POSITIVE (run `27524789748`, 2026-06-15, branch feat/484-framework-versioning — a real `next build` failure inside the bundle image build; the check working as designed, and the strongest argument for eventually promoting it). Three are Docker Hub registry incidents: run `27687999615` 2026-06-17 (external leg — `docker/dockerfile:1` manifest 500), runs `27951828338` and `27955604996` 2026-06-22 (migrate leg — `library/postgres:16-alpine` manifest; external leg — `minio/minio:latest` manifest). In ALL THREE incidents every check already in `contexts` was GREEN — so promoting these four legs would have converted three transient registry blips into three repo-wide merge freezes that did not otherwise occur (threat D-1). Unlike the prod-build Playwright leg, no already-required check shares this exposure profile (a full docker-compose bring-up plus a multi-stage image build across four topologies), so promotion here adds a genuinely NEW availability surface to the merge path rather than reusing an accepted one.
$retain_advisory_from_slice_419.fix_first_revisit: Fix-first, then promote (P0-419-1 — a candidate with a dirty soak gets a fix-first note, never a forced promotion). Ordered: (1) harden `deploy/docker/test-self-host-bundle.sh` against registry flakiness (retry-with-backoff on image pull, and/or a GHCR pull-through mirror for the base images) so a Docker Hub blip stops reading as a bundle regression; (2) add the four matrix-named slice-061 stub-twins (`Self-host bundle · end-to-end (bundled|external|proxy|migrate)`); (3) verify both directions — one docs-only PR resolving the four stub contexts green AND one code PR resolving the four real contexts green; (4) re-soak ≥5 clean runs per leg post-hardening; (5) promote all four expanded contexts in ONE change (a partial promotion leaves the same hole). Tracked in `docs/audit-log/419-promote-advisory-checks-decisions.md` §Revisit list.

$merge_queue.$slice: 415 — adopt GitHub's native merge queue on `main` so a green PR no longer needs a manual `gh pr update-branch` rebase that re-triggers the whole ~13-minute suite. Declared here because this file is the source of truth for the merge bar on `main`. See docs/ci/MERGE_QUEUE.md and docs/audit-log/415-merge-queue-decisions.md.
$merge_queue.$why_this_key_is_dollar_prefixed: The merge queue is NOT expressible through the classic branch-protection REST surface this file is PUT to. Verified 2026-07-24 against the live API: `GET /repos/mgoodric/security-atlas/branches/main/protection` returns no merge-queue field, and GraphQL introspection of `UpdateBranchProtectionRuleInput` returns no merge-queue input (the only match for /merge|queue/ is `lockAllowsFetchAndMerge`). Merge queue is configured through the branch-protection UI checkbox or a repository ruleset (`merge_queue` rule type). Following this file's `$`-prefix annotation convention therefore keeps `scripts/apply-branch-protection.sh` working unchanged — the script strips every `$`-prefixed top-level key before the PUT (slice 127), so this block is declared intent plus the apply ritual, not wire format. Teaching the apply script to reconcile the merge queue through the rulesets API is on the slice-415 revisit list.
$merge_queue.$configuration_rationale: Tuning defaults, each recorded with rationale + a revisit trigger in docs/audit-log/415-merge-queue-decisions.md (D3). SQUASH matches the repo's existing squash-merge-to-main convention (CLAUDE.md 'Branching') and is the only method compatible with `required_linear_history: true`. minimum_entries_to_merge=1 keeps a lone PR from waiting on a batch that will never form on a solo-maintainer repo; the 5-minute wait window lets a second PR join a batch when one is queued behind it. maximum_entries_to_merge=5 and build_concurrency=5 bound the speculative fan-out so a bad head cannot invalidate an unbounded amount of in-flight CI. ALLGREEN (every entry in the group must be green) over HEADGREEN because HEADGREEN merges the whole batch on the head entry's result — with the slice-061 path filter in play that is exactly the shape of threat T-1. check_response_timeout_minutes=60 exceeds the observed ~13-minute suite with headroom for the CodeQL leg.
$merge_queue.$required_checks: The queue gates on `required_status_checks.contexts` below, reused VERBATIM — slice 415 adds no check and removes none (P0-1).
$merge_queue.$apply: Not applied by `scripts/apply-branch-protection.sh` (see `$why_this_key_is_dollar_prefixed`). Maintainer apply: GitHub → Settings → Branches → the `main` protection rule → check 'Require merge queue' → set merge method SQUASH, 'Only merge non-failing pull requests', build concurrency 5, min entries 1 / wait 5 min, max entries to merge 5, grouping ALLGREEN, timeout 60 min → Save. Then re-run `bash scripts/apply-branch-protection.sh` so the contexts list stays reconciled, and confirm `required_linear_history` and `enforce_admins` are still on.
$merge_queue.$strict_interaction: `required_status_checks.strict` is RETAINED as `true` by slice 415 (AC-3): the queue subsumes the strict up-to-date requirement, but flipping the merge bar for every PR is the maintainer's call, not an agent's, and retaining it is the fail-safe direction (a PR can still not merge stale if the queue is never enabled). GitHub may itself disable 'Require branches to be up to date before merging' when the merge queue is turned on — the two are mutually exclusive in the UI. If it does, the live config will drift from this file's `strict: true` and `branch-protection-drift-live` will surface it; reconcile by setting `strict` to `false` here in a follow-up commit and noting that the queue now owns that guarantee. Tracked on the slice-415 revisit list.

$required_checks_hygiene_oe651.$issue: OPENENGINE-651 (2026-08-02) — required-checks hygiene. ~30 open PRs, many BLOCKED with every real check green. Root causes verified empirically against the live check-suites API over the currently-open PR set (fixtures: #1515 #1516 #1517 #1525 #1543 #1536), NOT assumed from the workflow files. Three contexts were structurally broken as merge gates and are removed below; every check with real signal is retained. Trimmed 19 → 16 contexts.
$required_checks_hygiene_oe651.analyze_contexts_removed: `Analyze (go)` + `Analyze (javascript-typescript)` REMOVED from `contexts` — skip-but-required brick. Evidence: `.github/workflows/codeql.yml` (the advanced-setup workflow these two names came from) has been `disabled_manually` since the 2026-06-29 → 2026-07-24 decommission window; its last run is 2026-06-29. CodeQL DEFAULT SETUP was configured 2026-07-23 (`GET /repos/mgoodric/security-atlas/code-scanning/default-setup` → state=configured, 7 languages) and now posts the `Analyze (…)` check runs via the `github-advanced-security` app. Default setup does NOT emit per-language check runs on a PR that touches no analyzable-language file: on dependabot manifest-only PRs #1515/#1516/#1517 (go.mod / package.json bumps) the github-advanced-security suite completed `neutral` with ZERO check runs, so the two required contexts never reported and the PRs sat BLOCKED-forever. Nearly every dependabot PR is manifest-only, so this bricked the entire class. No in-repo stub-twin can fix a context owned by an external app whose skip decision (which languages a merge commit 'touches') is not reproducible from a dorny/paths-filter expression.
$required_checks_hygiene_oe651.analyze_replacement_ruleset: The CodeQL merge gate is NOT dropped — it moves to a repository RULESET using GitHub's purpose-built 'code scanning results' merge protection, which has exactly the semantics the raw contexts lack: it blocks when CodeQL finds alerts ≥ threshold on the PR, and PASSES when no analysis is expected for the change (the neutral-pass-on-legitimate-skip the OE-651 spec asks for). Declared in `$code_scanning_ruleset` below ($-prefixed: rulesets are a different API surface than the classic-protection PUT this file feeds; same convention as `$merge_queue`).
$required_checks_hygiene_oe651.gitguardian_removed: `GitGuardian Security Checks` REMOVED from `contexts` (required → advisory) — chronically wedgeable external app. Evidence: on PR #1525 the gitguardian check suite sat `queued` with no conclusion for 5+ days, so the required context never reported and the PR was BLOCKED with everything else green; `POST /check-suites/{id}/rerequest` returns 404 for the GitGuardian app, so a hung suite has NO remediation path other than pushing an otherwise-pointless commit. Safety is not dropped: (1) GitHub NATIVE secret scanning AND push protection are enabled on this repo (verified via `security_and_analysis`), enforced at push time — a stronger control than a PR status; (2) the GitGuardian app continues to scan and report on every push, it just can no longer wedge a merge when its backend hangs.
$required_checks_hygiene_oe651.dco_kept: `DCO` KEPT required. It reports on every PR and fails only when a commit genuinely lacks `Signed-off-by` — that is the check working, not a broken gate. The 2026-07-31/08-01 engine-fire PRs (#1543 #1536 …) are blocked because their commits are actually unsigned (28 of the last 30 main commits ARE signed; the regression is in the PR authors' commit flow, not in the gate).
